envelope.description: Shape of every WebSocket frame the daemon emits — both command replies and broadcasts. The `payload` member is replaced per-frame; broadcast entries below name the OpenAPI schema (in assets/openapi.yaml under components.schemas) that pins its structure.

fields.seq: integer (uint64) — monotonic daemon-assigned cursor; clients store the last received value and pass it back as `since` on subscribe to resume the stream after a reconnect
fields.kind: string enum (initial|change|refresh) — event family discriminator; default and dominant case is `change`
fields.topic: string — routing key the client subscribed to (broadcasts only; absent on command replies)
fields.type: string — discriminator naming the event family; matches the `name` field of the matching broadcast entry below
fields.ts: string — RFC3339Nano timestamp of the event; UTC
fields.payload: object — see the per-broadcast `payload` field for the schema reference

resume.description: Client → server: append `since: N` to a subscribe op to request replay of buffered events with seq > N matching the supplied topic patterns. Server → client: after the replay completes, the daemon sends one of two control frames. `{op:"replay_done", seq:N}` confirms the replay finished and carries the last-replayed seq (or the original `since` when nothing matched). `{op:"replay_lost", oldest_seq:M}` signals that `since` precedes the oldest buffered event — the client must take a fresh GET /snapshot to resync. The replay buffer ceiling defaults to 1024 events.

heartbeat.description: The daemon sends a `{"op":"ping"}` frame every ping_interval_seconds. Clients MUST respond with `{"op":"pong"}` within read_timeout_seconds or the connection is closed. Clients behind NAT or mobile-data proxies that drop idle connections faster than read_timeout_seconds should additionally issue their own `{"op":"pong"}` frames pre-emptively — the daemon accepts unsolicited pongs.

subscription_ack.description: After a `{op:"subscribe", topics:[...]}` or `{op:"unsubscribe", topics:[...]}` is processed, the daemon echoes one `{op:"subscribed"|"unsubscribed", topics:[...]}` frame carrying the topics the client just requested. Reconnect-after-failure logic can use this ACK to confirm the subscription set survived the round trip without needing to inspect daemon-side state. An empty topics array suppresses the ACK to keep no-op subscribes quiet.

command_schemas.description: Each command entry below may carry an `args` and a `result` field documenting its argument and return shape. `args` is an object whose keys are argument names; each value is a string of the form `<json-type>[?]` (with `?` marking optional fields). `result` follows the same conventions and may also be `"array"` or a fully-spelled object. Missing fields mean the command takes no arguments and/or returns an opaque object — the canonical source for the wire shape is then the matching Go handler under internal/north/rest/ws/.

commands.name: alarm_panel.journal

commands.description: Return the live status of a walk-test session on an alarm zone.
commands.name: alarm_panel.walktest_status

commands.description: List the alarm-control-panel entity projections (HA-state view incl. the master panel).
commands.name: alarm_panel.panels

commands.description: List alarm codes (operator). Codes are security material, so even the list is operator-gated; the argon2id hash and cleartext PIN are never returned.
commands.name: alarm_panel.codes_list

commands.description: Create an alarm code (operator). The cleartext PIN is write-only and hashed before persistence.
commands.name: alarm_panel.codes_create

commands.description: Replace an alarm code (operator). An empty PIN keeps the stored hash.
commands.name: alarm_panel.codes_update

commands.description: Delete an alarm code (operator).
commands.name: alarm_panel.codes_delete

commands.description: Server-pushed: an alarm zone's arm-state-machine transitioned (docs/alarm-concept.md §5).
commands.name: alarm.state_changed

commands.description: Server-pushed: a running exit/entry delay on an alarm zone ticked (once per second).
commands.name: alarm.countdown

commands.description: Server-pushed: an alarm zone's per-mode arm-readiness was recomputed (docs/alarm-concept.md §6.3). Carries the full per-mode map, not a delta.
commands.name: alarm.readiness_changed

commands.description: Server-pushed: an alarm zone entered `triggered` and an incident was opened (or re-adopted after a restart / reconnect).
commands.name: alarm.triggered

commands.description: Server-pushed: one enrolled notification output fired for an alarm — a deliberate, per-zone, mode-filtered notification signal (one-shot at fire time, never cancelled by a later silence).
commands.name: alarm.notification

commands.description: Server-pushed: a new entry was appended to the alarm engine's event journal. Payload carries the entry head; clients needing full detail call GET /alarm/journal.
commands.name: alarm.journal_appended

commands.description: Server-pushed: a walk-test session on an alarm zone recorded a sensor activation.
commands.name: alarm.walktest_progress

commands.description: Server-pushed: the alarm subsystem's health verdict changed (siren stop-verification, service degradations).
commands.name: alarm.health_changed

commands.description: Alarm-control-panel entity projection changed (state, availability, code policy, identity, or removal).
commands.name: alarm.panel_changed

commands.description: Server-pushed: an arm schedule elapsed with auto-arm off while the zone was not in the scheduled mode, so the engine notifies rather than arming (docs/alarm-concept.md §15 row 19).
commands.name: alarm.reminder
